newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks reach new heights in London.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks reach new heights in London.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks in London climbed to record highs on Wednesday, taking strength from the UK FTSE's index new all-time high and major gains in Hong Kong overnight.
The Hang Seng London reference index set a record 11966.75 points but slipped slightly to close at 11965.39, up 13.51 points on the day.
In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng index climbed 30.66 points to reach 11,951.88, its highest close since February 1994.
Banking shares were up while other stocks had remained at their Hong Kong levels, with the market underpinned by gains in th U.S. long bond, traders said.
The main focus of interest was the release of Sun Hung Kai Properties' year-end results, with net profit up 6.5 percent in line with market expectations at HK$11.04 billion.
But by 1430 GMT, SHK Properties, which had closed at HK$ 81.75 in Hong Kong, was down at HK$81.625, down HK$0.70.
Traders said the market had tracked the FTSE 100 index, which set a record 4,016.4 points on Wednesday.
